edit.statement: Every ziggurat was built of brick.
edit.subject: ziggurat
edit.scope: The stepped temple towers of ancient Mesopotamia and Iran, Sumerian to Neo-Babylonian and Elamite, and the material they were built of: a core of sun-dried mud brick, usually faced with baked brick. Egyptian and Mesoamerican pyramids are other classes. Some Assyrian towers had a stone revetment on the lowest stage, as at Nimrud; their bodies were still brick, so 'built of brick' holds and 'built of cut stone blocks' is still false. Deleting the rule takes with it the looser general belief that goes with it, not a strict rule since Assyrian palaces used stone, that Mesopotamian and Elamite temple building was in brick for want of stone; otherwise that belief would give the material back.
